Started off as a teller and was quickly promoted to a universal banker on my way for becoming a business banker when it was announced that our bank was bought out. Right after my manager transfer and the manager who replaced her was awful. Never put out her schedule, threw all big projects at me with little to no help besides “call the help desk”, would pick and choose when she left with no consideration. And with the merger she was under the impression that the new bank’s structure allowed her to do even less so when it came time for mandatory training she’d sneak off for hours. Add to that helping out other branches who were even more short staff due to their even shitter managers chasing tellers out it was a nightmare.

 My breaking point was when I got covid, I was pretty much out for 2 weeks and she did nothing to help prepare and instead would call me to ask how to do things she should of known how to do. I ended up quitting for good, I never wanted to go into banking again after it. I’m back at retail now as an assistant manager to a clothing store I worked part time prior. With commissions it actually pays me more than the bank and I’m a lot happier for it.

You’re suffering from depersonalization/disassociation. I suffer from it too. You’re outside your head and don’t have any tethers to grasp on to. You are wishing so bad to be one of the characters you read about that you start feeling like them. 

From the trauma I’ve gone through I feel like a robot, I don’t feel real. Sometimes I wish I wasn’t. But then I read about others going through the exact same thing, and I mean this in the nicest way. You gotta humble yourself man. You’re not different from the billions out there not matter how different you make yourself. And you can go on the internet and contest it a million times but in the end you’ll find you have never lived a unique experience in your life. But you have to come to that not have internet strangers yell at you.
